key_insight: On a fixed compact manifold, parallel transport convolution is continuous in L² under C² perturbations of the Riemannian metric, subject to the stated localization and transport-path conventions.
engineering_relevance: The theorem supports robustness to small geometric changes in manifold-based convolution models, but does not provide numerical error rates.
method: Bound perturbations of geodesics, parallel transport, Jacobi fields, and exponential maps.
Compare transported kernels using uniform estimates away from the cut locus and integral bounds near it.
Control changes in the Riemannian volume measure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a qualitative mathematical stability theorem, not empirical benchmarks or numerical evaluations.
watch_item: The guarantee assumes continuous signals and kernels localized to a sufficiently small normal neighborhood; discretized implementations require separate validation.
paper_title: Stability of Parallel Transport Convolution under Riemannian Metric Perturbations
